function.name: calculate_time
function.description: Calculates the time taken to cover a distance at a certain speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance.description: The distance to be covered in meters. This is a float type value.

speed.description: The speed at which the object is moving in m/s. This is a float type value.

round_to_nearest_second.description: Optional parameter to round the time to the nearest second.

message.content: I’m sorry—I don’t have access to a live clock, so I can’t tell you the precise current time. If you’re looking for your local time, it’s best to check a device on your end (phone, computer, wall clock) or use a reliable online world‑clock service.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What's the time right now?" We need current local time or UTC? Usually we can provide server's timezone. But as an AI with no real-time clock, but maybe we have system time. In this environment, I think we cannot fetch actual time; we might approximate using known timestamp of last update (but not accurate). According to policy, if uncertain about exact time, we should say we don't know.

We could respond: I'm sorry, I can't access real-time data. Provide general info like "I don't have live clock." That would comply.

Thus answer: Sorry, I do not have real-time capability.
